title: The output of orglens with --json
description: One line of JSON on the standard output: an envelope with the result of the command in `data`, or with `error` when the command failed. A consumer ignores fields it does not know. This file describes the output of the version of OrgLens it ships with.

schemaVersion.description: The version of the envelope. It changes only when a field is removed or changes its meaning.

command.description: The command that ran. Null when the command line was rejected before a command ran.

ok.description: True if `data` holds the result. False if `error` says why there is none. The exit code can be other than 0 when this is true.

warnings.description: What the user should know although the command did its work.

code.description: A stable code. A code is never renamed or reused. New codes are added with new features.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

hint.description: What the user can do about it.

details.description: Facts about the failure. The fields depend on the code.

root.description: The absolute path of the workspace folder.

created.description: The files this call created, relative to the workspace, with forward slashes.

existing.description: True if orglens.toml was already there.

sourceFields.description: A declared source. A field that is not set in orglens.toml is null.

excludeTypes.description: The metadata types a snapshot of the source leaves out (`exclude_types`), sorted. Empty: every type is read.
The metadata types a snapshot of the source leaves out (`exclude_types`), sorted. Empty: every type is read.

sandboxOf.description: The name of an org source.

repo.description: The repository folder, relative to the workspace.

paths.description: The folders of the repository that belong to this source. Null means all of it.

tracks.description: The name of an org or sandbox source.

snapshots.description: How many finished snapshots of this source the database holds: complete ones and partial ones.

unfinishedSnapshot.description: The snapshot of an org or a sandbox that is being taken, or that was interrupted. The next `snapshot` of the source continues it. Null if there is none.

chunksDone.description: How many chunks of the retrieve are stored or were given up.

chunks.description: How many chunks the retrieve has.

latestSnapshot.description: The latest finished snapshot, which is the one `coverage` shows. Null if there is none.

analysis.description: The analysis the snapshot has. Null for a snapshot that was not analysed: `orglens analyse` analyses it.

engineVersion.description: The version of the engine that analysed it.

file.description: The database file, relative to the workspace.

problem.description: What is wrong, when the state is not `ready`.

coverage.description: What a snapshot holds, per metadata type, what its analysis found, and everything that was observed while it was taken and analysed.

id.description: The number of the snapshot. It is never used again.

status.description: What was read, whatever the analysis found. `complete`: everything the source holds was read. For an org that is judged over the logic tier: something of a type outside it can be missing, and a warning of the stage `read` with `details.tier` = `other` then says what. `partial`: something is missing, and the issues of the stage `read` and the severity `error` say what. `running`: a snapshot of an org that is being taken, or that was interrupted and is continued by the next `snapshot`. `failed`: a snapshot of an org that was given up.

engineVersion.description: The version of the engine that took it.

apiVersion.description: The version of the Metadata API an org or a sandbox was read with, such as 66.0. Null for a source of the kind git.

commit.description: The full id of the commit whose content the snapshot holds. Null if the snapshot does not hold exactly that: a file that was read from disk differs from the commit that is checked out, or Git could not tell which commit that is. An issue says which.

files.description: The number of files in the snapshot.

bytes.description: The size of the files together.

types.description: One entry per metadata type, sorted by type.

type.description: The metadata type, as Salesforce names it.

listed.description: How many components of the type the source says it has.

retrieved.description: How many of them are in the snapshot with all their files.

analysed.description: How many components of the type the analysis read something of. 0 for a type that this version does not analyse, and for a snapshot that was not analysed. It can be more than `retrieved`: the analysis also counts what it finds inside the files of other components, such as the fields in the file of an object.

listing.description: `ok`: the source said which components of the type it has. `failed`: an org refused to say, so `listed` is not the true number. `unlistable`: Salesforce never lists components of this type, and they are not read yet. `excluded`: `exclude_types` of the source leaves the type out, so the org was not asked for its components and `listed` is 0.

packaged.description: How many of the components the org listed of the type are of a managed package installed in the org, as the org says with the prefix of the package and the state of an installed one. Always 0 for a snapshot of a repository.

analysis.description: The analysis of the snapshot: the components its files make up and the references between them. Null for a snapshot that was not analysed.

crossCheck.description: What the Dependency API of Salesforce said about the org, held against the analysis. Null if the API was not asked for the snapshot: a snapshot of a source of the kind git, one taken with --no-cross-check, and one taken by a version before the cross-check existed.

issues.description: Everything that was left out, went wrong or is uncertain: first what the reading observed, then what the analysis observed. A snapshot with an issue of the stage `read` and the severity `error` is partial. What a snapshot of an org lacks of a type outside the logic tier is a warning of the stage `read` with `details.tier` = `other`, and leaves it complete. An analysis with an issue of the stage `analysis` and the severity `error` is not complete.

impact.description: What refers to a component in one snapshot, directly or through other components, or what the component refers to. The answer says what it does not cover.

id.description: The number of the snapshot that was asked.

status.description: `partial`: something of the source is missing in the snapshot. `notCovered` says whether that matters for this answer.

finishedAt.description: When the snapshot was finished. UTC, as in 2026-01-31T09:30:00.000Z.

analysedBy.description: The version of the engine that analysed the snapshot.

component.description: The component that was asked about.

sameName.description: The keys of the other components of the same name, sorted. Only where the component was named by its name alone and the name fits an object and more, such as the file of the workflow rules of the object: the answer is about the object. Also where the name fits a flow and its definition and nothing else: the answer is about the flow. Empty for a name that fits one component, and for a key or a type with a name.

parts.description: How many components of the snapshot the component contains, at any depth: the fields and rules of an object, the elements of a flow. The answer is about them too, and none of them is a result.

elementOf.description: For an element of a flow: the key of the flow. A flow runs its elements, so for `incoming` the answer holds what refers to the flow too. Null for any other component.

direction.description: `incoming`: the results are what refers to the component. `outgoing`, with --outgoing: they are what the component refers to.

depth.description: The value of --depth. Null: no limit.

beyondDepth.description: True if the answer stops at `depth` and references lead further.

minConfidence.description: The value of --min-confidence. References less certain than this were not followed.

results.description: The components that were found, sorted by depth and then by key. For `incoming`, a flow is found beside an element of it that is found, at the same depth and by the reference of that element, and the answer goes on from the flow to what calls it. A flow that was found nearer keeps that way, and so does one that a reference of its own finds at the same depth, unless the way through an element is more certain. The flow of `elementOf` is no result.

key.description: The component key. It is the same in every source and every snapshot, and `impact` takes it as its argument.

type.description: The metadata type, as Salesforce names it.

name.description: The name as the source spells it. Null for a component the snapshot refers to and does not hold, such as a standard field.

file.description: The file that defines the component, inside the source. Null if no file of the snapshot defines it.

package.description: As `package` of the component that was asked about. For `incoming`, a result of a package is left out unless `impact --packages` keeps it.

depth.description: How many references lie between this component and the one that was asked about. 1: it refers to it directly.

confidence.description: The weakest confidence among the references of the chain that leads to this component. Among the shortest chains the most certain one is kept. A longer chain can be more certain, and is found with --min-confidence.

reference.description: The reference this component is found by: the one at its end of a shortest chain of references between it and the component that was asked about. For `incoming`, `from` is this component and `to` is one reference nearer. For `outgoing` it is the other way round. A flow refers to what its elements refer to: for `incoming`, `from` of a flow can be an element of it, and for `outgoing`, the nearer end can be an element of a flow that is a result of the depth before. The nearer end is a result of the depth before, which holds the next reference of the chain. At depth 1 it is the component that was asked about, something that one contains, or the flow of an element that was asked about, and the chain ends.

packagesLeftOut.description: For `incoming`: how many components of managed packages refer to the component, directly or through other components, and are left out of `results`. The walk goes on through them, so the nearer end of the reference of a result can be such a component. 0 with `impact --packages`, and always 0 for `outgoing`, where a component of a package is a target and stays.

unresolved.description: For `outgoing`: the references to a name that has no key, so that no component stands for it. Always empty for `incoming`.

from.description: The key of the component the reference stands in.

type.description: The metadata type of the target.

name.description: The target as the source writes it.

kind.description: What the reference says about its two ends.

origin.description: Where the reference was learned from.

confidence.description: How certain the reference is, strongest first: confirmed, probable, possible.

resolution.description: `resolved`: the target is a component of the snapshot. `external`: it lies outside the snapshot, such as a standard field. `dynamic`: it is decided at run time and known in part. `unresolved`: it was named and not found.

file.description: The file of the reference, inside the source. Null for a reference that Salesforce reported without a place.

column.description: Columns start at 1 and count UTF-16 code units.

depth.description: The depth a component with this name would have.

newerVersions.description: The flows of the answer whose active version, which the snapshot holds, has a newer version beside it, such as a draft, sorted by flow: the flow that was asked about or the flow of the element that was, and the flows among the results. The newer version is not analysed, and the answer does not hold what it would change. Only a snapshot of an org can know of one.

active.description: The number of the active version, which is the one the snapshot holds.

newer.description: The state of the newer version, as its file names it, such as `Draft`.

complete.description: True if nothing is known that the answer could miss: the two lists of `notCovered` are empty and its four counts are 0. False says that the answer is what was found, and that `notCovered` names what could not be looked at.

notCovered.description: What the answer does not cover.

notAnalysed.description: The types of the snapshot that no analyser read, or that the analysis reads only in part, sorted by type: `ApexClass` and `ApexTrigger`, of which only the types their members use are read (decision record 0084). A component of such a type may refer to the component that was asked about, and not be in the answer. For `incoming`: not a type whose components can name no type of the answer, of the component, of what it contains, of the results or of a type that stays (decision record 0073). For `outgoing`: only the types of the component, of what it contains and of the results, because what a component refers to does not depend on other types.

partial.description: The analysed types of which the snapshot holds less than the source has, or whose listing failed, sorted by type. A type the analysis reads is among them also when the snapshot holds nothing of it.

readErrors.description: How many errors the reading had, without those that the coverage of their type tells: a type that could not be listed, and components that were not retrieved. A file or a folder could not be read, and what is missing may be of an analysed type. A warning of a snapshot of an org about something outside the logic tier (`details.tier` = `other`) is counted too if one of its `details.types` is a type the answer covers. Every type this version analyses is of the logic tier, and no snapshot is known to hold such a warning.

analysisErrors.description: How many errors the analysis had: a file that could not be read or placed, or a component that could not be analysed.

analysisWarnings.description: How many warnings of the analysis can bear on the answer: a name that was not read, a path that was not followed, a formula that was not read as a whole, or a part of a file that was not found. Each can hide a reference from its component. For `outgoing`: a warning of the component, of what it contains, of a result or of an element of a flow of the answer. For `incoming`: a warning of any other component, and a path that was not followed only where its names can be in the answer: a field of such a name, a record type, or an object where the path ends at one (decision record 0074). A warning about no component counts for every answer. The count is of the warnings that bear on the answer directly, not of one that bears only through a component another missing reference would bring. For an answer that covers flows, the warnings `FLOW_VERSION_UNKNOWN` of the reading are counted too: such a flow was analysed as a version that may not be the one that runs. They make `complete` false and leave `mayMiss` as it is.

notHeld.description: For `outgoing`: how many of the component and the results the snapshot refers to and does not hold, such as a standard field or a component of a package. What they refer to is not known. Always 0 for `incoming`.

mayMiss.description: True if something of the source was not read that the answer claims to cover: `notCovered.partial` is not empty, or `readErrors` or `analysisErrors` is not 0. The exit code is then 5. A type that is not analysed yet does not make it true, and neither does a warning of the analysis.

key.description: The component key. It is the same in every source and every snapshot, and `impact` takes it as its argument.

type.description: The metadata type, as Salesforce names it.

name.description: The name as the source spells it. Null for a component the snapshot refers to and does not hold, such as a standard field.

file.description: The file that defines the component, inside the source. Null if no file of the snapshot defines it.

package.description: The prefix of the managed package installed in the org that the component is of, as the org lists it with the state of an installed package. A part of a component, such as an element of a flow, is of the package of the component. Null for a component of the org's own, also of the org's own namespace, and for every component of a snapshot of a repository.

impactStep.description: One reference: the component it stands in, the component it names, and where it stands.

from.description: The key of the component the reference stands in.

to.description: The key of the component it names.

kind.description: What the reference says about its two ends.

origin.description: Where the reference was learned from.

confidence.description: How certain the reference is, strongest first: confirmed, probable, possible.

resolution.description: `resolved`: the target is a component of the snapshot. `external`: it lies outside the snapshot, such as a standard field. `dynamic`: it is decided at run time and known in part. `unresolved`: it was named and not found.

file.description: The file of the reference, inside the source. Null for a reference that Salesforce reported without a place.

column.description: Columns start at 1 and count UTF-16 code units.

type.description: The metadata type, as Salesforce names it.

listed.description: How many components of the type the source says it has.

retrieved.description: How many of them are in the snapshot with all their files.

listing.description: As in the coverage: `failed` if an org refused to list the type, `unlistable` if Salesforce never lists it, `excluded` if the configuration of the source leaves it out.

engineVersion.description: The version of the engine that analysed the snapshot.

components.description: The components of the snapshot, with the parts the analysis found inside files and the objects that are only named.

complete.description: False if an issue of the stage `analysis` has the severity `error`: a file of the snapshot could not be read or placed, or a component could not be analysed. The exit code of `snapshot` and `analyse` is then 5.

origins.description: One entry for each origin of references that this version analyses, in the order of the reference vocabulary.

origin.description: Where the references come from, such as `parser:xml`, `parser:formula` or `parser:flow`.

components.description: The components the analyser looked at. For `parser:formula`: the components that hold a formula or a default value. For `parser:flow`: the flows and their elements.

failedFiles.description: The files the analyser tried to read and could not. For `parser:formula`: the files with a formula that was not read as a whole, whose names are recorded as `probable`. For `parser:flow`: the files of flows.

unresolved.description: How many of them are `unresolved`: a custom name that no file of the snapshot defines and that is not of a package. A standard name and a name of a package that the snapshot has no file of are `external` and are not counted here.

pathsNotFollowed.description: The paths of names it could not walk to their end. What stands behind the point where it stopped has no reference.

crossCheck.description: How the Dependency API of Salesforce was read for a snapshot of an org, and what the comparison of its rows with the analysis found. The rows are no references of OrgLens: no answer of `impact` is made from them.

state.description: `whole`: no answer shows that a row is missing. `partial`: rows are missing, or may be, because a query was cut off or failed, or because rows were asked for component by component and nothing shows that the org listed every component. A reference that Salesforce knows and the analysis missed can then go unseen. `none`: the org answered no query, and nothing was compared.

requests.description: The requests that were sent to the org for it, with those that asked for the versions of the flows.

queriesCutOff.description: The queries that were cut off. One kind is a query whose answer holds half as many rows as one query gives at most, or more, or says that it does, with no smaller part to ask for. The other kind is a query whose answer was taken as whole and lacks a row that another query gave, and that it had asked for as well. The queries for the groups of components of one part of the rows are counted as one query where a row that the part gave did not come again with them.

queriesFailed.description: The queries that failed and whose rows no other query gave.

queriesNotProven.description: The queries near the limit of rows whose rows were asked for component by component, for more components than one query can name. Every row of a component the org listed was read. A row of a component it did not list would be missing, and nothing shows whether there is one.

code.description: The code of the first failure, such as INVALID_TYPE for an org without the API, TIMEOUT, or REQUESTS_USED_UP when the reading stopped at its limit of requests. Null if the state is `whole`.

comparison.description: What the comparison found. Null if nothing was compared: the state is `none`, the snapshot is not analysed, or the analysis it has was made by a version whose comparison this version cannot show. It is made again with every analysis, from the rows the snapshot holds.

crossCheckComparison.description: A row names two components. It is matched to two components of the snapshot by the ids the org listed them with. A name is taken only where there is no id: for a standard object, which the API names in the place of an id, and for a component the org listed without one. A row from a flow carries the id of a version of the flow: it is matched by the ids the org named for the versions of each flow, the active, the latest and every other one, and else by the id it listed the flow with, which is that of its latest version. `rows` is the sum of `rowsNotAnalysed`, `rowsNotMatched`, `rowsNotHeld`, `rowsOtherVersion` and `rowsCompared`. `pairs` is the sum of `agreed`, `coveredByPart` and the length of `missed`.

rows.description: The rows of the API the snapshot holds.

rowsNotAnalysed.description: The rows from a component of a type this analysis did not read, or read only in part, as `ApexClass` and `ApexTrigger`. They are not compared.

notAnalysed.description: The same per type, sorted by type. The type is the metadata type where the row could be matched or names one, and the type the API writes otherwise.

rowsNotMatched.description: The rows from a component of an analysed type of which one end is no component the org listed. They are not compared.

rowsNotHeld.description: The rows from a component of an analysed type that the snapshot does not hold or that was not analysed. They are not compared.

rowsOtherVersion.description: The rows from a version of a flow that is not the one the snapshot holds, such as a draft beside the active version, or an older version that a deploy left behind. The snapshot holds the active version where it has the note `FLOW_NEWER_VERSION` for the flow, and else the latest one. They are not compared.

pairs.description: The different pairs of components the compared rows are. A pair of a component with itself is not counted.

agreed.description: The pairs the analysis has as well.

coveredByPart.description: The pairs to an object for which the analysis has a reference from the same component to something the object contains, such as a field of it, and none to the object itself.

missed.description: The pairs Salesforce reports and the analysis lacks, sorted. Each is an issue of the stage `analysis` with the severity `error` and the code REFERENCE_MISSED, so the analysis is not complete.

onlyOrgLens.description: The pairs the analysis has, of a kind the API is known to report, for which no row was compared, sorted. Either the analysis found a reference that is none, or the API left one out, or the row is one that is missing (the state is `partial`) or could not be matched (`rowsNotMatched`). They are no issues.

notReported.description: The pairs the analysis has without a row, of a kind the API does not report, per reason, sorted by reason. They say nothing against the analysis.

reason.description: `standard-field`, `standard-object`: the reference is to something Salesforce provides. `inactive-rule`: it is from a validation rule that is not active. `default-value`: it is in the default value of a field. `lookup`, `lookup-filter`, `roll-up-summary`, `controlling-field`, `value-set`, `display-field`: it is that part of the definition of a field or an object. `workflow-rule`: it is from a workflow rule. `workflow-action`: it is from an email alert, an outbound message or a task of a workflow rule. `field-update`: it is from a field update, and not in its formula. `custom-metadata`: it is from a record of a custom metadata type, and not to the type of the record. `record-type`: it is from a record type. `subflow`: it is from a flow, to a flow it starts or overrides. `name-in-text`: it is from a flow, and only a text names it, such as the name of a record type a condition compares a text with. `global-variable`: it is from a flow, to a field of a custom setting or a custom permission that only formulas of the flow name. `action-override`: it is from an object, to a Visualforce page, a Lightning component or an s-control that overrides one of its actions. `report-type`: it is from a report type. `quick-action`: it is from a quick action. `other`: any other reference from the definition of a component. Reasons can be added.

crossCheckPair.description: A component, and a component it refers to, by their keys.

stage.description: `read`: observed while the source was read. `analysis`: observed while the files of the snapshot were analysed.

code.description: A stable code in upper case. Codes can be added.

component.description: The key of the component an issue of the analysis is about, such as `CustomField:invoice__c.total__c`. Null for an issue that is about no single component, and for every issue of the reading but `FLOW_NEWER_VERSION`, `ACTIVE_FLOW_NOT_RETRIEVED` and `FLOW_VERSION_UNKNOWN`, which hold the key of the flow they are about.

details.description: Facts about the issue. The fields depend on the code.

sourceLink.description: The Salesforce CLI login that was set for a source.

login.description: What was written to .orglens/local.toml: the alias or the user name that was given.

username.description: The user name of the login.

orgId.description: The id of the org the login belongs to, if the Salesforce CLI knows it.

declaredOrgId.description: The org id the source declares. With null, nothing says which org is meant.

sourceCheck.description: What the check of a source found: of an org or a sandbox, or of folders of a repository. `kind` says which.

via.description: `jwt-env`: a private key from the environment. `linked`: the Salesforce CLI login that `orglens source link` set for the source. `org-id`: the one Salesforce CLI login that belongs to the org the source declares.

alias.description: The alias of the Salesforce CLI login, if it has one.

username.description: The user name of the Salesforce CLI login. Null for a login with a key: there it comes from a secret.

id.description: The id of the org, as the org states it: 18 characters.

instanceUrl.description: The address of the org. Null for a login with a key.

apiVersion.description: The API version OrgLens uses with this org: the newest it offers, as in 66.0.

declaredOrgId.description: The org id the source declares. With null, nothing says which org is meant, and any login is accepted.

complete.description: True if a snapshot taken now would be complete. False: the exit code is 5.

commit.description: The full id of the commit a snapshot taken now would name, or null if it would name none.

dirs.description: The folders of the source, relative to the repository. One that could not be read is named in an issue.

bytes.description: The size of the files together.

issues.description: Everything that was observed. One of severity `error` would make a snapshot partial.

ok.description: False if a check failed. The exit code is then 1.

id.description: A stable name of the check.
